title: The Agent gives ZM's D7 retention in its memo file in Julia's Drive as 10.47%, as 10.59%, or as both (two figures or a 10.47%-10.59% span); a longer figure rounding to 10.47% or 10.59% also passes. A one-decimal figure passes only when the memo gives, anywhere in it, any one of its own backers: for 10.5%, 2,607 installs; 273 retained players; 16 cohort rows starting 2025-07-28; the cohort weeks 2025-07-28 to 2025-09-15; or the end week 2025-09-15; for 10.6%, 2,267 installs; 240 retained players; 14 cohort rows starting 2025-07-28; the cohort weeks 2025-07-28 to 2025-09-08; the end week 2025-09-08; or the KPI sheet ('ZM KPI snapshot', Vincent's sheet) named as its source (an end-week backer needs only its end week; any other row or week backer may be worded any way that fixes its first and last week, a start week plus a count of 8 weeks for 10.5% or 7 weeks for 10.6% fixes both, 2025-07-24 counts as the 2025-07-28 start only for a week span written with its end week, while a row or week count must start at 2025-07-28, and the backer must match the figure's own set; an install count rounded to the nearest hundred, 2,600 for 10.5% or 2,300 for 10.6%, also counts). A one-decimal figure stated with its own backer counts as naming 10.47% (for 10.5%) or 10.59% (for 10.6%) under every rule in this row. 10.5% anywhere in a memo that names 10.47% as the retention, or 10.6% anywhere in a memo that names 10.59%, is a rounding, not a bare figure or another figure. A bare 10.5% or 10.6% fails (10.5142%, 10.5454%, 10.4625%, 10.5792%, 10.635%, 10.63% and 10.61% also round to them). A figure is named as the retention when the memo calls it ZM's D7 retention or gives it as its answer. Another figure offered as ZM's D7 retention, alone, as an alternative, or side by side with 10.47% or 10.59% when neither is named as the retention, fails; a figure the memo ties to a different method, platform or range of cohort weeks, a source's own label for a different statistic ('D7 mean', 'average', 'median') counting as a different method (a different source alone is not enough: a figure the memo ties only to the warehouse or the KPI sheet, with no different method, platform or range of cohort weeks, must itself be 10.47% or 10.59%), and does not offer as a possible value of the retention, while naming 10.47% or 10.59% as ZM's retention is context (a figure other than 10.47% or 10.59% joined to the answer with 'or' is an alternative even when tied to a different method, platform or range of cohort weeks; 10.47% and 10.59% joined to each other with 'or' give both)
justification: Multi-source: Robert's method (install-weighted, mature cohorts with a D14 figure, both platforms pooled; Slack) over Vincent's 2025-07-24 cut-off (Sheets note) on the warehouse table (Snowflake) gives 10.47%, and off the KPI sheet 10.59%; both are fair.
evidence: Sources: C090N54TG79/1759167008.881274 ('install-weighted D7, not a simple mean of the cohorts. Mature cohorts only, meaning cohorts that have a D14 figure, both platforms pooled'); f_4e21b203a62910bdae0353 note ('use only cohort weeks starting on or after 2025-07-24'); ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION. Warehouse: 16 rows, weeks 2025-07-28 to 2025-09-15, 2,607 installs, 27,297.69/2,607 = 10.4709% (273/2,607 = 10.4718%). KPI sheet: 14 rows, weeks 2025-07-28 to 2025-09-08, 2,267 installs, 10.5859% (240/2,267 = 10.5867%). OE 29 calls either fair; either or both pass, with or without a stated method. Accept: 10.47% or 10.59% (or a longer figure rounding to either), both, or a 10.47%-10.59% span; 10.5% with any one of 2,607 installs, 273 retained players, 16 cohort rows starting 2025-07-28, the weeks 2025-07-28 (or 2025-07-24) to 2025-09-15, or the end week 2025-09-15 (its only other paths to 10.5% are the recorded iOS-only simple mean and the 18-row pooled median from 2025-07-21, 10.485%); 10.6% with any one of 2,267 installs, 240 retained players, 14 cohort rows starting 2025-07-28, the weeks 2025-07-28 (or 2025-07-24) to 2025-09-08, the end week 2025-09-08, or the KPI sheet ('ZM KPI snapshot', Vincent's sheet) named as its source (the other paths to 10.6% on that sheet are the recorded iOS-only simple mean, 10.63%, and the sheet's rows 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-25 install-weighted and pooled, 10.5792%, the D30-only cohorts); a backer anywhere in the memo; an end-week backer needs only its end week; any other row or week backer in any wording that fixes its first and last week (a 2025-07-28 start plus 8 or 7 weeks fixes both; a 2025-07-24 start counts only with the end week written, since 16 rows or 8 weeks from the cut-off also describes the KPI path with the 2025-07-21 week, 10.5454%) and matches the figure's own set; an install count rounded to the nearest hundred (2,600 or 2,300) also counts; a backed one-decimal figure counts as naming its two-decimal figure under every rule in this row (so a backed 10.5% and a backed 10.6% together are both figures, and other figures tied to a different method, in a memo that names a backed figure as the retention, are context); 10.5% anywhere in a memo naming 10.47% as the retention, or 10.6% anywhere in a memo naming 10.59%, is the same figure. Fails: a bare 10.5% (also 10.5142% with no D14 filter, 10.5454% from the KPI sheet with the 2025-07-21 week, 10.4625% iOS-only simple mean) or a bare 10.6% (also 10.5792% D30-only, 10.635% 16-row median, 10.63%/10.61% iOS-only simple means); another figure offered as the retention, alone, as an alternative, or side by side with 10.47%/10.59% when neither is named as the retention.
